subject: Pricing stability request — 3yr commit (price lock + uplift cap + renewal protection)
messages:
From: Kyle Rogers <kyle@acmecloudware.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing for 3-year commit — price stability and renewal protection

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Acme is planning to consolidate inference spend and we are evaluating a 3-year committed agreement. Two items are critical for procurement and exec sign-off: a firm price lock for the committed term (no increases beyond agreed uplift caps) and a renewal protection clause so we don’t see outsized step-ups at first renewal.

High level ask: 3-year commitment on committed ARR of $2.1M/year, with a maximum annual uplift no greater than 12–15% and renewal protection that limits increases on the first renewal to the same uplift cap. Can Redwood do this as part of a standard commercial package, and if so what approvals are required?

Attaching our draft SOW for context.

Thanks,
Kyle Rogers
VP Finance, Acme Cloudware
Attachments: Acme-SOW-v1.pdf (application/pdf)
From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Kyle Rogers <kyle@acmecloudware.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing for 3-year commit — price stability and renewal protection

Kyle — appreciate the clarity, and excited about the potential to partner. I need to confirm a few internal sensitivities before giving a final answer.

Short answers:
- We can consider a multi-year price lock tied to committed ARR, but anything beyond our standard uplift guidance requires Deal Desk + Finance sign-off.
- Renewal protection (limiting first renewal increases to a cap) is something we can include as an exception, again requires approval.

To move fast, could you confirm: 1) whether the $2.1M/year is guaranteed (minimum commit) vs expected usage; 2) a preferred uplift cap (12% vs 15%); and 3) whether you need the renewal protection to apply to the first renewal only or to subsequent renewals as well.

I’ve looped in our deal desk lead and finance to evaluate. I’ll follow up once we have an internal recommendation.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Marissa / Ben — forwarding thread with Acme. They want a 3-year committed agreement at ~$2.1M/year and have two contract asks that are outside standard auto-renew language:

1) Price lock for the 3-year committed term (no increases to the committed-rate beyond an agreed annual uplift cap).
2) Renewal protection: on the first renewal, increases must be limited to the same uplift cap — they want predictability.

My recommended options to present to the customer:
- Option A (conservative): 36-month price lock, uplift cap = 12% annual, renewal protection applies to first renewal only; requires finance sign-off and a 1.1x volume commit threshold.
- Option B (balanced): 36-month price lock, uplift cap = 15% annual, renewal protection limited to first renewal, no extra volume threshold but 90-day notice window for renewal pricing.

Attachments: Proposed-MAP-v1.pdf (draft commercial summary).

Can you review and flag what needs exec approval (discounts / term deviations / legal signoff)? Rishi — please advise on economics and acceptable uplift ceiling tied to 3yr commit.

Thanks,
Laura

Thanks Laura — quick read. I like Option B as the negotiable public offer: 36 months, uplift cap 15%, renewal protection for first renewal only, 90-day notice. That keeps the close motion easy for AE.

That said, the 3-year timeframe plus that uplift cap materially increases our exposure if usage spikes. We should trade: either require a minimum spend ramp (e.g., minimum committed ARR year-over-year) or tighten the uplift to 12% if they want no minimum.

Ben / Rishi, from a deal desk perspective this is an exception vs our standard 12-month price protection. Rishi — can you weigh in on financial guardrails and whether we can do 15% with the $2.1M commit? If yes, what approval level do we need?

Marissa Cole
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Pricing for 3-year commit — Exec approval requested (Acme Cloudware)

Reviewed the economics and ran a quick sensitivity. Key notes:
- 3-year price lock with an uplift cap is permissible if we get a minimum committed ARR (guaranteed) equal to the $2.1M/year or a multi-year prepay schedule. If ARR is only an expected range, exposure becomes material.
- Uplift cap: recommend 12% as our ceiling for no-minimum deals. We can go to 15% but only with a minimum contractual floor of 1.05x in year 2 and 1.1x in year 3 (annualized committed floor).
- Renewal protection: OK to include a clause limiting increases on the first renewal to the uplift cap if legal signs off on wording that preserves our right to re-evaluate for material changes (MC clause).

Attached: deal-econ-summary.xlsx (stub).

Decision required: Exec approval to permit the deviation from standard 12-month price protection and to accept the proposed uplift/commit trade. I approve the following conditional path:
- Approve Option A if customer signs the guaranteed commit floor (1.1x by year 3) — uplift cap 12%.
- Approve Option B (15% uplift) only with prepay or higher committed floors.

Please advise if you want me to loop in finance exec (CFO) for sign-off or take this through pricing committee.

-Rishi
Finance, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Pricing for 3-year commit — Pricing and next steps (approved path)

Kyle — quick update and next steps. Thanks for the patience.

We’ve completed internal review. Summary of the approved commercial path: 
- Term: 36 months (price lock for committed-rate)
- Committed ARR: $2.1M/year guaranteed (contractual minimum)
- Uplift cap: 12% annual maximum during committed term (Option A, approved by Finance)
- Renewal protection: First renewal can only increase pricing by up to the uplift cap and must provide 90 days’ notice; legal will include a material-change carve-out.

Conditions: the customer must agree to the contractual minimum (guaranteed ARR) or a prepay schedule; legal redlines required (attached: redlines-terms.docx). Once legal agrees, we’ll route the final commercial terms through DocuSign.

Next steps for Acme: please confirm acceptance of the committed ARR and sign off on the SOW redlines. I’ve attached a draft of the concession language (redlines-terms.docx) and included the DocuSign link for the Term Sheet: https://docusign.com/embedded/sign/abc123

If you want, we can set up a 30-minute call with Marissa and Rishi to walk the procurement/legal team through the guardrails.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this.
